searchText: <Andrew_Beal> Hi RollCall Community - Just a reminder that OpenZeppelin/Forta will be presenting RIP-7614 on tomorrow's RollCall #3. This proposal is seeking to add a new precompile that exposes the full call stack to called contracts. The authors are very interested in feedback from rollups, so I hope everyone has an opportunity to review 7614 and think about feedback/questions prior to the call. Post RollCall, we are also interested in setting up one-on-one discussions with rollup teams to dive deeper into specific concerns and willingness to adopt. https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/rip-7614-expose-call-stack-to-contracts/18535 ^ this seems like it would weaken optimization techniques by exposing more implementation details on tomorrow's rollcall, I want to sync up on the status of L2 4844 testing. so, if you have been working on this, it'd be great to get at least someone from your team on the call <mratsim> I'm not even sure how to start proving this in a zkEVM. And example from the EIP: > Moreover, blackhats deploy attack contracts before launching the attack and that gives a time frame to scan and detect the malicious contract. If the attack transaction does a DELEGATECALL from a proxy to the attack contract, to call the victim contract, then the msg.sender observed by the victim contract is the proxy contract (and not the actual malicious attack contract). The call stack breaks this evasion by exposing the DELEGATECALLed addresses in the call stack. For instance, this defense can be circuimvented by having a single tx where there is firstly a contract deployed and then called. This could be done through private mempool not giving enough time for anyone to react.
